title: Assert frequency separately in index-combination regression tests
answers: Does assert_index_equal verify the resulting index frequency?
How should I test concat retaining frequency when inputs are reordered?
How can a DataFrame constructor test catch lost holiday-aware frequency?
body:
Assertion: Frequency-sensitive regression tests explicitly compare result.freq with expected.freq after tm.assert_index_equal, which does not check frequency; see pandas/tests/frame/test_constructors.py:TestDataFrameConstructors.test_constructor_dict_of_series_datetimeindex_freq.
Fixture: Combine overlapping ranges in an order that creates an intermediate gap later filled by another input; a CustomBusinessDay with holidays exercises frequency metadata that values alone cannot recover.
Ordering: Cover sort=True, sort=False, and omitted sort as in pandas/tests/reshape/concat/test_datetimes.py:TestDatetimeConcat.test_concat_datetimeindex_freq_order_independent and TestDatetimeConcat.test_concat_timedeltaindex_freq_order_independent. Expected frequency depends on final ordering: nonmonotonic results retain freq=None.
applies: Regression tests for frequency metadata in datetime-like index unions used by concat and DataFrame construction.
